newsitem.title: MONACO: SOCCER SHOWCASE-MONACO LOOK TO WRAP UP TITLE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-MONACO LOOK TO WRAP UP TITLE.

text.p: Monaco, having digested their UEFA Cup disappointment, want a victory at home against Marseille on Saturday as they bid to wrap up the French first division title as soon as possible.
"I'm really in a hurry for us to be champions," said coach Jean Tigana, whose team are 11 points clear of second-placed Paris St Germain with five games to play.
If they win and PSG fail to beat bottom club Nice at home on Sunday, Monaco will be crowned champions for the sixth time.

Monaco will also be looking to avenge a 3-1 defeat at Marseille's Velodrome stadium when the two sides met in November, their first league clash since the former European champions' enforced relegation in 1994 over a match-rigging scandal.

A league clash between the two sides has been a highlight of the French league season over the last decade since Marseille's confirmation in the 1990s as a leading international force and Monaco's growth into another top European side.
There is the added spice of 12th-placed Marseille still looking for their first away win of the season.
"The whole team will play to the full at Monaco. The squad would love to finish the season notching up at least one away victory," Marseille's Bulgarian midfielder Yordan Lechkov said.
But Saturday's match, despite its potential for producing a good, exciting game, has been slightly devalued by international call-ups, injuries and Marseille's mediocre return to the top flight.
Monaco will be missing Nigerian striker Victor Ikpeba, Scotland midfielder John Collins, Belgium's captain Enzo Scifo and Swiss forward Marco Grassi -- all on World Cup duty.
But, with a richly talented squad, they can still field a strong side against Marseille with defender Gilles Grimandi and playmaker Ali Benarbia back after UEFA Cup suspension.

Marseille have veteran captain Jean-Philippe Durand, France under-21 midfielder Ludovic Asuar and Italian central defender Ivan Franceschini out with injuries and forward Mehdi Ben Slimane away with the Tunisian national team.

Their German international goalkeeper Andreas Koepke is doubtful with a pulled muscle, although he is available. If he is fit, he plans to join Berti Vogts' squad after Saturday's match for a World Cup qualifier against Ukraine.
"It will be a last minute decision," a member of the club's medical staff said.
Striker Marc Libbra will play with a protective bandage after surgery last Saturday on an ear injury.
"Monaco, they're the Formula One of the championship. But we do rather well against the good teams," said Marseille's top scorer Xavier Gravelaine, who has 13 league goals.
Marseille, who have had poor results against lowly teams, drew 0-0 away to Auxerre, Bordeaux and PSG and beat Monaco 3-1 and the defending champions 3-0 at home last year.
This year they have beaten Bastia 1-0 at home, but crashed 4-0 at Bordeaux and 1-0 at home to Strasbourg. They face PSG in their last home match on May 17.
Marseille have not won at Monaco since the end of the 1991-92 season when a 3-0 victory helped them to their fourth consecutive first division title.
In their only two subsequent meetings at the Louis II stadium, Monaco won 1-0 in 1992-93 and they drew 0-0 early the following season.
